title: Component Spec (v0)
description: Machine-checkable pin-level constraints for an electronic component. Consumed by sim_harness/static_check.py to detect wiring bugs against a schematic netlist. v0 focuses on the classes of bug that appear at Layer 1 of the verification pyramid (abs-max violations, wrong series component, forbidden direct connections). Later versions will grow additional constraint kinds as new bug classes are discovered.

spec_version.description: Schema major version. Bumped on breaking changes.

mpn.description: Manufacturer Part Number. Used as the canonical key for this component; the checker matches schematic symbols to specs by MPN (via a component Value or MPN property).

package.description: Physical package (e.g. TSSOP-28, DFN-8). Informational; not used for matching.

local_path.description: Path to the cached datasheet, RELATIVE TO THIS SPEC FILE'S DIRECTORY. Convention: keep the PDF alongside v*.json under components/<MPN>/ so the whole component travels together.

net_families.description: Names for classes of net that constraints reference symbolically (e.g. 'AGND' → any net matching one of these regexes counts). The checker resolves a constraint's target_net_family by looking up the family here and testing every net in the design against its patterns.

patterns.description: Regex patterns (Python re syntax, matched with re.fullmatch against the net name; leading '/sheet/' is stripped first).

ac_model.description: Small-signal (AC + DC operating-point) behavioral model for this IC. When present, the runner emits an auto-generated SPICE .subckt for the topology and instantiates it in place of any per-pin dc_model on the ac_model-owned pins. Per-pin dc_checks still evaluate against the solved node voltages. Consumed by Layer 3a (op-point), Layer 4a (AC sweep), and future Layer 4b (loop-stability). Complements — but does not replace — a vendor-supplied `behavioral_spice_subckt` (which wins if both are given).

behavioral_spice_subckt.description: Path to an external SPICE .subckt (e.g. a vendor-published behavioral model). When present, the runner `.include`s the file and instantiates the named subckt with terminals in the given order. Overrides `ac_model` and per-pin `dc_model` for the mapped pins.

xspice_model.description: Reference to an XSPICE code-model (.cm shared library). Runner loads the .cm before parsing the netlist (via .spiceinit for subprocess backend, via early exec_command for pyspice backend), emits a `.model` line with the given parameters, then instantiates the IC as an `A<ref>` XSPICE device. Use for behavior that can't be expressed with parametric topologies (Layer 5c) or a plain .subckt: chip state machines, custom analog devices, event-driven digital logic. Precedence: overrides `behavioral_spice_subckt`, `ac_model`, and per-pin `dc_model`/`transient_model` on the mapped pins.

modeling.description: Meta-information about what THIS spec models and how faithfully. Purely informational for the runner today, but consumed by capability-suitability checks: a scenario can declare `requires_capabilities: [...]` and the runner refuses to run against a spec that doesn't claim them all. Optional; omit entirely for specs that don't want to make claims (they just don't get the pre-flight suitability check).

provenance.description: Audit trail of how this spec was created — extractor runs, datasheet revision hashes, per-field consensus from the multi-agent pipeline. Optional. NOT a confidence score — records what was done, not what it means.

oneOf.description: Multiple pad identifiers that all resolve to this logical pin. Try each in order until one is found in the netlist. Use when the datasheet pad numbering (e.g. 1-8 for a DFN-8) differs from the schematic symbol's pin identifiers (e.g. G/D/S for Q_NMOS) — list the datasheet-native pad first, then the schematic-native alias.

index.description: Pad number/name as it appears in the KiCad symbol/footprint. May be an array of aliases when datasheet and schematic use different conventions.

name.description: Datasheet pin name (e.g. 'CS', 'SLOPE', 'MODE'). Informational for the checker; used to make violation messages readable.

voltage_range.description: Absolute-maximum voltage range on this pin, from the datasheet's abs-max table. NOT the operating/nominal range — v1 will add a separate operating_voltage_range field for that. v0 status: parsed but not yet exercised by an abs-max intersection rule.

current_range.description: Absolute-maximum operating current, if published. Informational at v0.

constraints.description: Topological constraints that the pin's net must satisfy.

may_be_unconnected.description: If true, the checker will not warn when this pin is unconnected.

dc_model.description: How this pin behaves in Layer-3a DC operating-point analysis. Omit for the safe default (`high_z` — pin has no explicit driver, node voltage is determined by whatever else is on its net).

dc_checks.description: Layer-3b assertions on the pin's DC voltage. Evaluated after the operating-point solve. Each check compares the pin's solved node voltage against a datasheet-known threshold or expected value; a failure indicates the surrounding design has a wrong divider, wrong reference, missing enable network, etc. Move IC-specific knowledge from scenario `expected` blocks into these — one project-independent check, reused across every scenario that uses this IC.

transient_model.description: Layer-5c time-domain behavior of this pin. Used by `.tran` runs; ignored by DC (`dc_model` covers that) and AC (`ac_model` covers that). Emitted as an ngspice B-element (behavioral source) with the topology's expression. When present, suppresses per-pin `dc_model` emission during transient runs (the transient_model IS authoritative for time-domain behavior).

notes.description: Free-form. Use for constraints the schema can't yet express — those patterns get upstreamed into structured fields over time.

reference.description: Net family name that the voltages are relative to. Defaults to 'GND'.

constraint_must_connect_through.description: The pin's net must reach the named target family exclusively via a series two-terminal component of the specified type (and, optionally, value range). Fails if the pin is on the target net directly, or if it reaches the target through the wrong component type or a value outside the allowed range.

value_range.description: Inclusive [min, max] range in SI base units (ohms / farads / henries). Optional.

to_net_family.description: Name declared in the parent spec's net_families.

constraint_forbidden_direct_connection.description: The pin's net may not match this family directly. Weaker than must_connect_through — use when the pin is allowed to float or to sit on a signal net, just not on the named rail.

oneOf.description: Pin has no explicit driver; node voltage is determined by other components on its net.

Pin is a Thevenin-equivalent source. Provide either voltage_v (a known fixed voltage) or follows_rail (a symbolic rail class the scenario maps to a schematic net). impedance_ohms defaults to 0 (ideal source); set to a positive value for a weak internal pull-up/pull-down.

voltage_v.description: Fixed voltage this pin sources, relative to GND. Use for internal LDO outputs (LM5176 VCC=7.6V), fixed references (VREF pins), etc.

follows_rail.description: Symbolic rail class the scenario maps to a specific schematic net (e.g., 'OUTPUT' → 'VOUT_12V'). Use for regulated output pins whose voltage the scenario must dictate because Layer 3a cannot close the switching loop.

impedance_ohms.description: Thevenin series impedance. 0 = ideal source. Positive values model weak internal pull-ups/pull-downs (e.g., voltage_v: 0, impedance_ohms: 100000 for a 100kΩ internal pull-down).

oneOf.description: Pin is a Norton (ideal current) source. Use for pins that source or sink a specific current independent of the external voltage — internal current mirrors, charge-current-set outputs, soft-start charge currents, etc. Cannot be expressed as Thevenin.

current_a.description: Magnitude of the current in amps. Positive number; use `direction` to specify sense.

direction.description: `out_of_pin`: current flows from the pin into the external circuit (a source, e.g. LM5176 SS pin's 5µA charge current). `into_pin`: current flows from the external circuit into the pin (a sink).

oneOf.description: Pin voltage must equal a specific value within a tolerance. Use for feedback pins that regulate against a datasheet reference (LM5176 FB=1.2V), fixed reference outputs, or any node whose steady-state DC value is fully determined by the surrounding network.
Pin voltage must be strictly above a threshold. Use for enable / start-up / rising-edge thresholds — verifies the surrounding divider or driver actually crosses the trip point.
Pin voltage must be strictly below a threshold. Use for shutdown / disable / falling-edge thresholds.

Pin voltage must lie in [min_v, max_v]. Use for absolute-max range checks (subsumes the voltage_range abs-max concept for DC), or valid-operating-window checks (e.g. LM5176 MODE pin's 1.38–2.22V CCM+hiccup window).

Canonical single-pole op-amp: differential input × A0 → single-pole rolloff at f_p = GBW/A0 → low-impedance output. Suitable for most general-purpose op-amps whose datasheet advertises A0 (open-loop DC gain, dB) and GBW (gain-bandwidth product, Hz). Output impedance defaults to 100 Ω if unspecified. The runner emits one `.subckt` per matched IC (numbers baked in) and instantiates it as `X<ref> <inp_net> <inm_net> <out_net> OPAMP_SP_<ref>`.

a0_db.description: Open-loop DC gain in dB (e.g., 100 for 100000 V/V). Corresponds to the datasheet's 'Large-signal voltage gain' or 'A_VOL'.

gbw_hz.description: Gain-bandwidth product in Hz. Corresponds to the datasheet's 'Gain-Bandwidth Product' or 'Unity-Gain Bandwidth'.

output_z_ohm.description: Open-loop output impedance in Ω. Matters for stability with capacitive loads (Layer 4b). Datasheets rarely publish this — 100 Ω is a defensible default for general-purpose parts.

pins.description: Which pin (by index — either the numeric pad or a schematic-symbol alias like 'IN+') plays each role. Power supply pins (V+, V-) are intentionally omitted from the canonical model — the ideal-source assumption is fine at Layer 3/4a. If a spec sets rail-following dc_models on V+/V-, those still emit (they just don't participate in the ac_model subckt).

pin_index_ref.description: A pin's index as it appears in the schematic symbol. Must match one of the values in that pin's `pins[].index` (aliases are honoured — the runner tries each candidate).

behavioral_spice_subckt.description: Reference to an external SPICE .subckt file (typically a vendor-published behavioral or macromodel).

path.description: Path to the .lib / .sub / .cir file containing the .subckt definition, RELATIVE TO THIS SPEC FILE'S DIRECTORY. Convention: keep the file alongside v*.json under components/<MPN>/.

subckt_name.description: The name after `.subckt` in the file (SPICE is not case-sensitive; the runner emits verbatim).

terminals.description: Ordered list of subckt terminals paired with the schematic pin they map to. Order MUST match the .subckt declaration order — SPICE X-lines are positional. Every schematic-side pin_index must resolve to a pin in the netlist (aliases honoured).

subckt_terminal.description: Terminal name as it appears in the subckt declaration (for readability only; the runner ignores the string and uses list order).

oneOf.description: Fixed current source into the pin until pin voltage reaches `clamp_v`, then holds. The canonical soft-start ramp: with an external cap C to ground, pin voltage ramps linearly at dV/dt = current_a/C until reaching clamp_v. Emitted as B-element: `I = current_a * (V(pin) < clamp_v ? 1 : 0)` (or the mirror for into_pin direction).

current_a.description: Magnitude of the source current. Positive; use `direction` for sign.

direction.description: `out_of_pin` = current flows from pin into external cap (charges cap toward positive rail). `into_pin` = current flows into pin (discharges cap toward negative rail).

clamp_v.description: Voltage at which the internal current source cuts off. Typically the chip's reference voltage (V_REF for soft-start feedback pins).

oneOf.description: Pin holds at `before_v` until time `delay_s` after t=0, then transitions to `after_v` with the given rise time. The canonical POR / boot-delay behavior. Emitted as a PWL voltage source. NOTE: `delay_s` is relative to simulation t=0, not to any external trigger — for trigger-based delays, use a different topology once we add one.

rise_time_s.description: Transition duration. Default 1 ns for a near-ideal edge.

oneOf.description: Pin output is `high_v` when V(sense_pin) exceeds `threshold_v`, else `low_v`. The canonical PGOOD-style output. Optional `stable_for_s` adds a first-order filter delay before the output can rise, modeling the 'input must be stable for N µs before PGOOD asserts' behavior common on power-sequencing ICs. Emitted as B-element voltage source.

sense_pin.description: The pin whose voltage is compared to threshold_v. Must resolve to a pin_index (int or symbolic name) on this same component.

stable_for_s.description: First-order filter time constant on the output. 0 = ideal instantaneous response; positive values delay assertion by ~this many seconds. Use to model PGOOD's 'input must be stable' delay.

cm_path.description: Path to the .cm shared library. Relative paths are resolved from the spec file's directory. Absolute paths (e.g., `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ngspice/analog.cm` for ngspice's built-ins) also work.

model_type.description: The XSPICE model-type name defined in the .cm (e.g., `gain`, `d_and`, `climit`). Runner emits `.model <ref>_<model_type> <model_type> (...)`; the per-instance name is derived to avoid collisions when the same IC appears twice.

model_params.description: Key/value parameters for the .model line — formatted as `key=value` in emission order. Values may be numbers or strings (strings pass through untouched, e.g. '1n' for time with SI suffix).

connections.description: Ordered list of XSPICE terminal connections. Order MUST match the model's declaration order (A-lines are positional). Two connection kinds supported at v0: `differential` (emitted as `%vd(pos neg)`; if `neg_pin` is omitted, GND is used) and `single` (emitted as a bare node name, for digital / event-driven signals). Array connections (`[a b c]`) not yet supported — defer until needed.

neg_pin.description: Optional; if omitted, GND is used as the reference.

disposition.description: `claimed` = extractor asserted, no cross-check. `verified` = human or automated check confirmed spec matches datasheet. `failing` = known-wrong pending fix (paired with a note).

capabilities.description: Positive assertions about what this spec models. A scenario can require a subset of capabilities via its `requires_capabilities` field; runner does a pre-flight suitability check. Silence on a capability doesn't mean 'not modeled' — it means 'unclaimed'. Add tags only for what the spec actually contributes. Each item may be a bare string (defaults to `disposition: claimed`) or an object with disposition + note.

scope.description: What this simplification is attached to. `component` = whole-IC-level. `pin` = specific pin. `capability` = the named capability tag. `net_family` = a named net class on this IC.

target.description: The pin index, capability tag, net-family name, or component MPN this simplification refers to. Use empty string for scope=component (implicit).

kind.description: `stubbed` = tied off to a placeholder (e.g. AGND merged into GND). `idealized` = ignores second-order effects (e.g. clamp is sharp not smooth). `approximated` = uses a simpler formula than the datasheet specifies. `best_guess` = datasheet vague, extractor made a plausible choice. `omitted` = deliberate non-modeling of a known-real behavior.

note.description: Explain what was simplified and why. Should be specific enough that a downstream user can decide whether it blocks their use case.

simplifications.description: Documented deviations from full datasheet fidelity. Sparse by design — only entries where someone actually decided something worth recording. Silence on a subject means 'unspecified', not 'faithful'.

capability_tag.description: Enum of capabilities the harness knows how to check. Grows as new layers and topologies ship. Naming: `l<layer><suffix>_<bug-class>`. Adding a new tag is additive; old specs stay valid.

extractors.description: Number of independent extractor agents in this run.

datasheet_sha256.description: Hash of the PDF the extraction was run against — if the PDF changes, extraction is stale.

extractor_runs.description: Chronological log of extraction attempts. Newest last.

extractor_consensus.description: `unanimous` = all extractors agreed. `arbitrated` = judge picked from disagreeing extractors. `disputed` = judge couldn't confidently pick; best guess recorded.

field_consensus.description: Per-field/per-pin consensus from the most recent multi-agent extraction. Keys are JSON pointers (e.g. `pins/3/dc_model`) or free-form dotted paths. Enum is primary axis; raw counts kept alongside for meta-analysis.

constraint_paired_with.description: This pin forms a differential pair with the named partner pin on the same component. v0 status: informational only — the checker parses this constraint but does not act on it. Planned v1 semantics: (a) error if partner pins share a net (differential short); (b) error if the partner nets' abs-max envelopes cannot satisfy max_differential_v (requires abs-max intersection engine).

max_differential_v.description: Maximum |V(this) - V(partner)| the pair tolerates. Informational at v0.
